intro: VEIL® ARAY holds every perforation at one diameter on an even grid. It is the plainest surface in the range, which is its use: where the ceiling should be a material and nothing more.
VEIL® BRUT sweeps its perforations from large to small in one continuous grade across the panel. It gives a wall direction and depth, and it is the most graphic surface in the range.
VEIL® CHAM runs chamfered slots on a close diagonal, so the panel reads as a rake of light rather than a grid. It suits a long wall or corridor that needs to feel like it is going somewhere.
VEIL® CHEV steps its perforations into V-shaped bands that meet point to point. The chevron is familiar enough to stay calm, and it carries a large plane without tiring.
VEIL® CZEC sets small perforations on a regular grid and keeps them there. It is a restrained, almost industrial field, and border and corner panels close an installation off cleanly.
VEIL® FALL staggers large and small perforations row by row, reading as scattered fall. It has movement without direction, which suits a ceiling that should feel alive but not point anywhere.

VEIL® FLAK breaks the surface into graded square apertures that resolve from fine to open like a halftone. Up close it is a grid; from a distance a gradient, and that shift is what carries a tall space.
VEIL® FUME scatters its perforations in loose, irregular drifts and leaves broad areas of panel unbroken between them. It is the quietest of the set, and it belongs where the ceiling should recede.
VEIL® MESH opens the field into a mesh, with perforations meeting edge to edge. It is the most open surface in the range and the one that lets a lit cavity read through most evenly.

VEIL® NOCT scatters small perforations sparsely, like points of light on an unbroken field. Lit from behind it reads as a night sky; unlit it is nearly solid, which makes it the most adaptable surface here.

VEIL® RAIN draws its perforations into vertical slots of varying length, falling the height of the panel. It is directional and quiet at once, and it reads well where a round hole would look mechanical.
VEIL® RAST drifts hole size across the panel in slow diagonals, so the surface gathers into soft blocks of light and thins between them. Read from across a room it is a texture, not a motif.
VEIL® RAYS runs its perforations in diagonal ranks across the full face, in a close or an open spacing. The two densities can be run together to shift a space gradually.

VEIL® RGYL sets its perforations in crossing diagonal bands, so the surface reads as an argyle lattice rather than a field of holes. It gives a ceiling a figure without a motif large enough to date it.
VEIL® RING runs graduated perforations in alternating diagonal bands to form a chevron weave. It carries the feel of woven cloth onto a hard ceiling, softening a room without competing for attention.
VEIL® SERR ramps perforation size up and drops it sharply, repeating the step across the panel. The break is deliberate and visible, and it gives a plane an edge a smooth gradient cannot.
VEIL® SHIM grows its perforations along one diagonal and fades them along the other, massing into wedges. It gives a plane weight and lift, and suits a ceiling that should feel like it is moving.

VEIL® SMOG holds a fine, closely pitched perforation across the whole face, broken only by sparse larger marks. It is close to a flat material with a grain, for when nothing should draw the eye upward.
VEIL® TIDE pulses perforation size along one axis, so bands of open and closed alternate across the panel. It gives a long run of ceiling a rhythm that can be turned with or against the room.
VEIL® WARP weaves larger perforations through a fine field to form an open diagonal lattice. The two scales working against each other give the surface depth, so it holds up at close range.
